chk_problem.label: accurate
chk_problem.poster_evidence: This work investigates whether commercial quadrupeds like the Unitree Go2 can operate effectively on tiled roofs—a novel, unexplored environment combining steep inclines, smooth surfaces, and discrete structural features.
chk_problem.reason: The poster accurately states the research problem of investigating the feasibility of using quadruped robots on tiled roofs.

chk_method.label: accurate
chk_method.poster_evidence: A custom test rig simulating a German-style tiled roof (Frankfurther Pfanne) was built to evaluate the Unitree Go2’s performance.
chk_method.reason: The poster accurately describes the method of using a custom roof test rig to evaluate the robot's performance.

chk_data.label: accurate
chk_data.poster_evidence: A custom test rig simulating a German-style tiled roof (Frankfurther Pfanne) was built to evaluate the Unitree Go2’s performance. Three core locomotion tasks were tested: balancing on increasing inclines, get-up/lie-down sequences in multiple orientations, and incline walking. Motion capture (OptiTrack) tracked foot slippage via reflective markers.
chk_data.reason: The poster accurately mentions the Frankfurter Pfanne roof tiles and the OptiTrack motion capture system used for data collection.

chk_setup.label: accurate
chk_setup.poster_evidence: Three core locomotion tasks were tested: balancing on increasing inclines, get-up/lie-down sequences in multiple orientations, and incline walking. Motion capture (OptiTrack) tracked foot slippage via reflective markers. Friction coefficients were measured using a UR10e force-torque sensor. All trials were automated via Python using WebRTC, with the robot set to standard walking mode at 1.0 m/s.
chk_setup.reason: The poster accurately details the experimental setup, including the tasks, control via Python, and speed of 1.0 m/s.

chk_primary_result.label: accurate
chk_primary_result.poster_evidence: Incline walking showed a quadratic increase in slippage with incline angle (p < 0.001), with critical failures occurring regularly at 25°.
chk_primary_result.reason: The poster accurately states that slippage increased quadratically and critical failures occurred regularly at 25°.

chk_secondary_result.label: accurate
chk_secondary_result.poster_evidence: Standing balance failed at 27.58° ± 0.72°, primarily due to front-limb slippage. Get-up/lie-down succeeded only up to 11° (head-up/down) and 7° (sideways), failing when the center of mass exited the support polygon.
chk_secondary_result.reason: The poster accurately reports the critical standing angle of 27.58° ± 0.72° and the get-up/lie-down limits of 11° and 7°.

chk_baseline.label: accurate
chk_baseline.poster_evidence: The Go2 failed to meet manufacturer claims of 40° slope capability.
chk_baseline.reason: The poster accurately compares the robot's performance against the manufacturer's claim of a 40° slope capability.

chk_conclusion.label: accurate
chk_conclusion.poster_evidence: Friction coefficients were 1.144 (flat) and 1.430 (curved), suggesting theoretical inclines >48°, but dynamic performance fell far short—highlighting control and stability as key bottlenecks.
chk_conclusion.reason: The poster accurately concludes that unmodified quadrupeds are not currently capable of safe operation on roofs due to control and stability bottlenecks.

chk_limitation.label: accurate
chk_limitation.poster_evidence: Testing should expand to other platforms, variable speeds, weather conditions, and payloads.
chk_limitation.reason: The poster accurately identifies the limitations of the current study (ideal conditions, single speed, no payloads, single platform) by framing them as areas for future work.
